summary_paragraph: A woman with type 1 diabetes was admitted for acute nausea, vomiting, periumbilical abdominal pain, and diarrhea. She presented with diabetic ketoacidosis due to missed insulin, with an initial anion gap of 22 that improved to 12 after IV fluids and insulin. Her symptoms resolved rapidly, and she tolerated oral intake. Stool testing for C. difficile was negative, and celiac antibody testing was also negative. Her pain improved with supportive care, and she was discharged home with a prescription for loperamide and plans for an outpatient colonoscopy to evaluate for irritable bowel syndrome or inflammatory bowel disease. She was stable at discharge with no complications.
